scenarios.title: Our half-ice change signal
scenarios.objective: Recognize the puck-release and change routine in a named game model.
scenarios.briefing: This activity uses the Hockey Canada U9 half-ice change rule: on the designated change signal, release the puck and leave for the next unit while play continues. The signal has just sounded while YOU control the puck. The full-rink picture shows player relationships only, not the exact half-ice layout or bench. Navy attacks the +x end; gold attacks the -x end. The full rink is an orientation map for this small activity.
cues: The designated change signal was stated.
YOU still own the puck at this instant.
The next unit waits off the illustrated area.

scenarios.limits: Static experimental illustration. Coaching responses and reference positions are suggestions. No skating, tactical mastery or learning transfer is certified. An adult may read questions and record spoken reflections. Explicit half-ice-model demonstration. Not current local-policy verification; no U9 full-ice transition date is used.

questions.prompt: Who must release the puck at this instant?

options.text: Gold1, who does not have it

questions.explanation: YOU are the declared puck owner when the change signal sounds.

questions.prompt: Which instructions belong to this named routine?

options.text: Finish a long attack before changing

questions.explanation: Those actions follow the quoted model in the briefing. Local program applicability still needs review.

options.text: The next unit continues the activity

questions.explanation: This describes the model, not a moving trace or a universal rule for all games.

questions.prompt: Does the whole game stop for this stated change?
questions.explanation: The briefing states that play continues under this half-ice model.

questions.prompt: Imagine a different practice says whistle means stop and listen. Which instruction applies there?
questions.explanation: Signals need context. A practice stop and this game change routine are different.

questions.prompt: How can you know which whistle routine the coach is using?
questions.explanation: Listen to the activity instructions and ask if unclear. The scenario does not establish a rule for every U9 program.

questions.prompt: For the next branch, imagine Gold1 reaches the puck after YOU release it. In this change routine, what should YOU do?

options.text: Continue leaving for the next unit
Chase Gold1 to win it back first
Stay until Navy2 gets the puck

questions.explanation: The designated signal still means release and change in this named activity. A new puck owner does not cancel the change instruction.

questions.prompt: What helps the next unit take its turn in this activity?

options.text: Release the puck when the change signal sounds
Leave using the route the coach explained
Take the puck with YOU to the waiting players

questions.explanation: Release control and make room for the next unit. Use the real activity’s exit route; the picture does not show the bench.

questions.prompt: This picture does not show the waiting area. How should YOU find the exit route for your real game?

options.text: Use the route the coach explained; ask if unclear
Head for whichever boards look closest

questions.explanation: The coach or official can show the actual change route. Do not invent an exit from a picture that only shows player relationships.

questions.prompt: Why should YOU leave after the signal even when the attacking end is nearby?
questions.explanation: In this named half-ice routine, the signal gives the next unit its turn while play continues. Being near the attacking end does not mean finishing another attack first. Other game formats can use different routines.
